title_en: Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Civil Dispute Cases involving the Protection of Well-known Trademarks

articles.content_en: Article 1. For the purposes of this Interpretation, a well-known trademark refers to a trademark that is well known to the relevant public within the territory of China.

Article 3. In the following civil dispute cases, the People's Court shall not examine whether the trademark concerned is well known:
(1) where the establishment of the alleged act of trademark infringement or unfair competition is not based on the fact that the trademark is well known;
(2) where the alleged act of trademark infringement or unfair competition is not established because it does not meet other elements prescribed by law.
Where a plaintiff brings an infringement action on the ground that the domain name registered and used by the defendant is identical or similar to its registered trademark, and the e-commerce conducted through such domain name for transactions in relevant goods is sufficient to cause misidentification by the relevant public, the case shall be handled in accordance with the provisions of item (1) of the preceding paragraph.

Article 4. When determining whether a trademark is well known, the People's Court shall, on the basis of the facts proving that it is well known, comprehensively consider the factors prescribed in paragraph 1 of Article 14 of the Trademark Law, except where, in light of the specific circumstances of the case, it is sufficient to determine that the trademark is well known without considering all the factors prescribed in that Article.

Article 6. Where a plaintiff brings a civil action on the ground that the use of the accused trademark infringes the exclusive right to use its registered trademark, and the defendant raises a defense or files a counterclaim on the ground that the plaintiff's registered trademark reproduces, imitates, or translates its prior unregistered well-known trademark, the defendant shall bear the burden of adducing evidence for the fact that its prior unregistered trademark was well known.

Article 7. Where, before the occurrence of the alleged act of trademark infringement or unfair competition, a trademark was previously determined to be well known by a People's Court or an administrative department, and the defendant does not object to the fact that the trademark is well known, the People's Court shall recognize such fact. Where the defendant raises an objection, the plaintiff shall still bear the burden of adducing evidence for the fact that the trademark is well known.
Unless otherwise provided in this Interpretation, the People's Court shall not apply the rules of admission of evidence in civil actions to the fact that a trademark is well known.

Article 8. Where a trademark is well known to the public within the territory of China, and the plaintiff has provided basic evidence that its trademark is well known, or the defendant does not object, the People's Court shall recognize the fact that the trademark is well known.

Article 9. Where it is sufficient to cause the relevant public to be mistaken as to the sources of the goods using the well-known trademark and the accused trademark, or sufficient to cause the relevant public to believe that there is a specific connection, such as a license to use or an affiliated enterprise relationship, between the operators using the well-known trademark and the accused trademark, it constitutes "easily causing confusion" as prescribed in paragraph 2 of Article 13 of the Trademark Law.
Where it is sufficient to cause the relevant public to believe that the accused trademark has a considerable degree of connection with the well-known trademark, thereby weakening the distinctiveness of the well-known trademark, disparaging the market reputation of the well-known trademark, or improperly exploiting the market reputation of the well-known trademark, it constitutes "misleading the public, so that the interests of the registrant of the well-known trademark may be damaged" as prescribed in paragraph 3 of Article 13 of the Trademark Law.

Article 12. Where an unregistered well-known trademark for which a party requests protection falls under the circumstances provided in Articles 10, 11, and 12 of the Trademark Law where it may not be used or registered as a trademark, the People's Court shall not support the request.

Article 13. In civil dispute cases involving the protection of well-known trademarks, the People's Court's determination that a trademark is well known shall only serve as case facts and grounds for judgment and shall not be written into the main text of the judgment; where a case is concluded by way of mediation, the fact that the trademark is well known shall not be recognized in the mediation document.
Article 14. Where previous judicial interpretations of this Court are inconsistent with this Interpretation, this Interpretation shall prevail.
